tagline: Stanly County hills that go by the name Rolling Kansas.
intro: Out of Richfield the road follows Main Street, which becomes Millingport Road, then turns onto Bear Creek Church Road for the last 3.4 miles to the Cabarrus County line. It is 9.2 miles in all, about fifteen minutes.
The country is hilly, and with its turn-of-the-century farms and windmills it earned the nickname Rolling Kansas. The road winds through it with long views over the western Piedmont.

moments.title: Richfield
moments.text: The starting town began as Ritchie's Field, after the family who set up its post office, its sawmill and its streets.

moments.title: Bethel Bear Creek Church
moments.text: Near the end of the road the churchyard keeps tombstones from the 1820s, in one of the oldest cemeteries in Stanly County.

sources.label: NCDOT, North Carolina Scenic Byways guidebook, Rolling Kansas Byway
